Flutter code that needs to know reduced-motion reads MediaQuery.maybeDisableAnimationsOf(context) directly at the point of use (see voice_indicator.dart line 366: 'final bool stilled = MediaQuery.maybeDisableAnimationsOf(context) ?? false;'), which is the idiomatic equivalent of this hook's job, built into the framework rather than authored as a package-level utility.
api.web: usePrefersReducedMotion(): boolean returns true when matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches, with a false server snapshot for SSR-safety, per hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts lines 33-39.
api.note: This is exactly the case the RULES contract calls out: 'most components in this system never need this' because the blanket CSS rule in globals.css already collapses animation for CSS-driven motion (hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts lines 14-19); it exists only for JS-driven motion (canvas, rAF loops), a browser-specific escape hatch with a native Flutter equivalent (MediaQuery), not a missing capability.
